messages.subject: pheno has no name error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to run a SNP scan using a new csv file for my phenotypes. I've formatted it exactly as in the read cross file but I keep getting this error.

Can anyone help!

Thanks,
Anna.

messages.subject: Re: pheno has no name error
messages.body_plain:
The scan functions in R/qtl2 use the row names in the phenotype data and the genotype probabilities to ensure that the individuals are aligned. If the phenotype data is a vector without names you'll get an error "pheno has no names". If it is a matrix without row names, you'll get an error "pheno has no rownames". You need to I presume that this is the problem.

If the phenotype data are stored in a file with a column of individual IDs, you could read them into R with read_pheno(), and that might help to ensure that the names are there.

karl

messages.subject: snpprobs
messages.body_plain:
Hello Karl,

I was wondering what the reason was for coding snpprobs as a two columns for the probability of the two possibilities (A/B) when calculated using allele probabilities rather than just having a single probability for "A" since B would be 1 - prob of A if I understand the idea correctly.

Cheers
Senthil

messages.subject: Re: snpprobs
messages.body_plain:
We treat the SNP probabilities as a special case of the general multi-allelic probabilities. And SNP probabilities could be for genotypes AA,AB,BB, or just for alleles A,B.

There's no particularly reason. We'd save memory by dropping the last column, but some aspects of the software would be more complicated.

karl
